I now have the full picture of the implementation. Let me evaluate each requirement against the code.

The implementation is a minimal bookmark manager: an Express server with a JSON file store exposing GET/POST/PUT/DELETE for bookmarks (fields: `url`, `title`, `description`, `tags`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `id`), and a vanilla-JS frontend with a list, a search box, tag-chip filtering, and a create/edit modal.

Key observations from the code:
- No page-metadata fetching (no title/description/favicon/preview retrieval on save).
- No note field, no unread flag, no archived flag anywhere in server or client.
- Search is a plain case-insensitive substring match over title+url+description+tags — no `#tag` syntax, no boolean/parenthesis/phrase parsing.
- POST always pushes a new record (no duplicate-URL convergence).
- No autocomplete, no bulk actions, no snapshots, no import/export, no bundles, no settings, no user-selectable sort (fixed by createdAt desc).
